title: Topical preparations for preventing stretch marks in pregnancy
findings: RR .74 (.53–1.03); insufficient high-quality support. Many formulations combine actives.
funding: Trial funding unknown except Osman lotion donation and Taavoni 2011 no funding reported; review-level disclosure not extracted
limitations: Old search; heterogeneous products and substantial heterogeneity; not proof no topical can help

title: Cocoa butter lotion for prevention of striae gravidarum: a double-blind, randomised and placebo-controlled trial
findings: No clear prevention benefit.
funding: ET Browne Drug Company supplied active and placebo lotions per Cochrane trial characterization; cash and sponsor role unknown
access: Primary abstract and P3-01 funding passage
limitations: In-kind support is a tie, not proof of biased results; negative trial retained

title: The effect of bitter almond oil and massaging on striae gravidarum in primiparaous women
findings: Incidence 20% massage+oil, 38.8% oil alone, 41.2% control.
limitations: Nonrandomized or allocation methods need verification; no massage-only group; bitter almond oil product safety/formulation not established; not home instructions

title: The Effect of Topical Virgin Coconut Oil on Striae Gravidarum Prevention and Severity: A Randomized Controlled Trial
findings: Incidence 25% vs 45%; modified SGAS 1.8 vs 2.6 at 32 weeks and 1.4 vs 2.2 at 6 weeks postpartum; no adverse effects reported.
funding: Not disclosed on accessible article landing page
limitations: Full allocation, attrition, denominators, protocol, outcome validation, harm ascertainment and sponsor disclosure unverified. No derived RR/CI; no universal safety claim.
authors: Ulya R, Sunesni, Suganda Y, Radhia MZ
adverse_events: None reported in abstract; ascertainment pending

title: Effects of Collagen Supplements on Skin Aging: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
population: Adult skin aging trials, not pregnancy prevention
findings: Positive overall estimates; no clear benefit in non-pharmaceutical-company-funded or high-quality subsets.
funding: Review grant statement not retrieved; underlying trials separated by sponsor
conflicts: Authors Myung and Park declare none per publisher indexed disclosure
limitations: Funding subgroup significance differences are not a formal interaction test; indirect to pregnancy

title: Hydrolyzed Collagen for Skin Aging Meta-Analyses Are Unreliable
population: Adult skin aging trials in earlier meta-analyses
findings: Table 1 identifies SE/SD errors, incompatible instrument units and omissions. Hydration: 4/7 industry-funded significant, 0/2 nonsponsored. Elasticity: 10/13 industry-funded; all significant results from those, 0/3 nonsponsored. Dose meta-regression did not establish clear trend.
funding: Review grant support not established from inspected passages; underlying trial sponsorship counts reported
access: Full text selected Table 1, Table 2, Figure 1, discussion, disclosure
limitations: Not a new primary cohort; vote count not pooled effect; no pregnancy outcomes; authors' methodological critique should be checked against original trial data

title: Oral Collagen Peptides and Skin Rejuvenation: A Systematic Review and an Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
findings: SMD hydration .44 (.15–.73), elasticity .62 (.15–1.10), TEWL -.39 (-.62–-.16); structural antiaging evidence limited.
limitations: Overlapping trials likely with P3-05/06; instrumentation surrogate; no direct striae prevention

title: The effect of breastfeeding on breast aesthetics
findings: Pregnancy count, age, BMI, larger prepregnancy bra size and smoking associated with ptosis; breastfeeding not independent predictor.
limitations: Selection, recall and confounding; does not establish causal null or bra/exercise prevention

title: Assessment of breast volume changes during human pregnancy using a three-dimensional surface assessment technique in the prospective CGATE study
findings: Mean volume 420 to 516 mL; increase quartiles 41,95,135 mL.
funding: PubMed indexes non-US government support; exact source and commercial ties not verified
limitations: Volume not ptosis or cosmetic outcome; no preventative treatment comparison

title: Curl-up exercises improve abdominal muscle strength without worsening inter-recti distance in women with diastasis recti abdominis postpartum: a randomised controlled trial
population: 70 women 6–12 months postpartum; 12 weeks home exercise vs no intervention
findings: Strength MD +9 Nm (3–16) at 10 degrees; thickness +.7 mm (.1–1.3); IRD not worsened.
limitations: Specific program, late postpartum; cannot generalize to immediate postpartum, hernia or symptomatic complications

title: Impact of postpartum exercise on pelvic floor disorders and diastasis recti abdominis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
funding: UQTR research chair, Christenson Professorship, Alberta Innovates studentship (author support; underlying trial funding separate)
access: Full text results, figures 6–7 and funding footnote
limitations: Moderate UI/POP certainty; low overall rest IRD certainty; clinical important gap difference unknown; correction updates guideline title
correction_retraction_status: Publisher correction note: guideline title updated; full registry sweep pending

title: What is the evidence for abdominal and pelvic floor muscle training to treat diastasis recti abdominis postpartum? An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials and trial sequential analysis
findings: TrA-focused vs minimal/no intervention MD -.06 cm (-1.19–1.08).
limitations: Narrow comparison; heterogeneity; does not show exercise useless for strength or pain. Overlap with P3-11/13.

title: Non operative management of postpartum Diastasis Recti: a systematic review and metanalysis of randomized controlled trials
population: Postpartum structured programs vs standard exercise or no intervention
findings: Standard exercise comparator MD -9.59 mm (-13.45–-5.72); no-intervention comparator -6.87 mm (-10.51–-3.23); functional ODI improvement not clear.
limitations: High heterogeneity, site/measurement and co-intervention confounding; overlapping trials; do not infer ideal timing from subgroup comparisons

title: Pregnant women may exercise both abdominal and pelvic floor muscles during pregnancy without increasing the diastasis recti abdominis: a randomised trial
findings: 12-week targeted program with 6-week postpartum follow-up did not support universal prohibition.
limitations: Exact estimates and harms pending; do not imply universal clearance

title: Transversus abdominis and rectus abdominis activation exercises do not alter inter-recti distance in pregnant women: a randomised trial
population: Pregnant women; targeted TrA or RA vs general exercise
findings: 12 weeks; no substantial change in IRD or pelvic floor symptoms versus general exercise.
limitations: Sample, absolute effect, registration and adverse events still need extraction

title: Evaluation of Postpartum Pelvic Floor Physical Therapy on Obstetrical Anal Sphincter Injury: A Randomized Controlled Trial
population: OASIS; outcome table n19 PFPT and n24 control
findings: PFDI-20 median change -29.2 (IQR -58.3 to -4.2) vs 0 (-14.6 to 20.8) from 2–12 weeks, p=.002.
funding: Harvard Catalyst NIH UL1TR002541 and Harvard/affiliated academic centers; no funder role reported
access: Full text Table 2, acknowledgments and financial disclosures
limitations: Small sample, baseline imbalance, no objective manometry; IQR not CI; specific injury group

title: The Impact of Exercising on Pelvic Symptom Severity, Pelvic Floor Muscle Strength, and Diastasis Recti Abdominis After Pregnancy: A Longitudinal Prospective Cohort Study
population: 503 included; 424 completed questionnaire, 410 clinical assessment at 12 months
findings: Low-impact exercise associated with improvement in several recovery outcomes; stress UI remained common regardless of activity.
funding: Healthcare Committee Region Västra Götaland, Research and Development Centre Gothenburg and Södra Bohuslän; no funder influence reported
limitations: Self-selection/reverse causality; no causal exercise clearance; 32 high-impact at 3 months

title: Pushing limits: the acute effects of a heavy-load resistance protocol and supine exercise on fetal well-being
findings: Acute Doppler and fetal HR measurements generally reassuring; one symptomatic vena cava compression episode during supine exercise.
funding: Norwegian Women's Public Health Association, indexed PDF funding text; authors report no sponsor role. PDF not opened; full disclosure needs confirmation.
access: Indexed primary abstract and funding snippet
limitations: Acute measures not long-term pregnancy safety; selected trained population; no blanket clearance or fetal home monitoring
adverse_events: One symptomatic vena cava compression event

title: 2025 Canadian guideline for physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep throughout the first year post partum
findings: Aim to build gradually toward 120 min/wk MVPA; individual symptom-based progression; no adverse lactation signal in supporting reviews.
funding: Panel and funder disclosures pending; related review P3-11 author support checked
limitations: Canadian jurisdiction; compare ACOG and US guidance; not universal permission or deadline

title: Antenatal perineal massage for reducing perineal trauma
findings: Suturing RR .91 (.86–.96), episiotomy RR .84 (.74–.95); not guarantee no severe tear.
limitations: Older review; distinct from intrapartum massage; appropriate consent and clinical timing

title: Effects of acupuncture and stabilising exercises as adjunct to standard treatment in pregnant women with pelvic girdle pain
findings: Stabilising vs standard morning pain median difference 9 (1.7–12.8), evening 13 (2.7–17.5); acupuncture also favored in some outcomes.
funding: Vardal Foundation, Dagmar Foundation, Trygg-Hansa Insurance Company, Sahlgrenska University Foundation; no sponsor role reported
limitations: Mixed including insurer; not independent-only; no sham in this trial, see P3-22; compare same-cohort follow-up/harms separately

title: Acupuncture as an adjunct to standard treatment for pelvic girdle pain in pregnant women: randomised double-blinded controlled trial comparing acupuncture with non-penetrating sham acupuncture
findings: Cochrane review reports no clear benefit vs sham for pelvic pain or functional disability.
access: Indexed primary identity and Cochrane synthesis
limitations: Full primary outcomes and disclosures pending; no needle instructions

title: The efficacy of abdominal binder in women undergoing cesarean delivery: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
limitations: Scale and exact denominators pending; short-term support, not permanent waist shaping or DRA correction

title: Comparison of Silicone Sheets and Paper Tape for the Management of Postoperative Scars: A Randomized Comparative Study
findings: Subjective appearance VAS better for silicone at 6 and 12 months; exact clinical meaningfulness unresolved.
limitations: Paired design, not independent arms; closed/healed scar care per clinician, not open wound

title: Efficacy of topical silicone gel in scar management: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
findings: Some Vancouver Scar Scale component improvements at >=6 months.
limitations: Indirect to cesarean-specific outcome; underlying trial overlap with S118/119/121 pending

title: A prospective split-scar randomized controlled trial of post-operative silicone tape improves scar appearance
findings: Reported improvement with specific silicone dressing; detailed outcomes pending.
funding: Publisher funding page inaccessible; not verified
limitations: Do not assume cesarean-specific or endorse brand. Sponsor/product donation and paired effects need verification.

title: Compression stockings prophylaxis of emergent varicose veins in pregnancy: a prospective randomised controlled study
findings: No prevention of emergent varicose veins, but improved symptoms and less saphenous reflux in trial.
limitations: Not DVT prophylaxis evidence or individualized compression prescription; symptom relief distinct

title: Evaluation of the effectiveness of a broad-spectrum sunscreen in the prevention of chloasma in pregnant women
design: Uncontrolled prospective study with historical comparison
findings: 5 new cases (2.7%); historical comparison 53%, not concurrent randomized group.
funding: Not verified; manufacturer ties must be checked before product-specific claim
limitations: Historical comparator and selection; no causal risk reduction estimate, no brand recommendation

title: Investigation of exacerbating factors for postpartum hair loss: a questionnaire-based cross-sectional study
findings: Examined breastfeeding duration and other possible factors; does not establish causality or support weaning for hair.
limitations: Recall/self-report, confounding; no preventive product evidence; persistent/patchy loss needs evaluation

title: Topical Acne Treatments
findings: Avoid topical retinoids during pregnancy; some OTC active ingredients may be used when needed with stage-specific evaluation.
limitations: Do not generalize safety by ingredient to all concentration, route, or breast application; preserve hold RP001

title: Potential Risks with Certain Uses of Radiofrequency (RF) Microneedling — FDA Safety Communication
findings: Reports burns, scarring, fat loss, disfigurement, nerve damage; no incidence denominator.
limitations: No causal risk rate; no home or pregnancy aesthetic device recommendation

title: Urgent Maternal Warning Signs and Symptoms
population: Pregnancy and first year after delivery
findings: Urgent maternal warning signs require immediate medical attention.
limitations: Not exhaustive; no automated diagnosis or delay to urgent care

title: Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period
findings: Exercise encouraged in eligible pregnancies; strenuous activity in elite athletes requires risk discussion and provider input.
limitations: Current reaffirmation and exceptions need release check; no clinical clearance

title: Interventions for preventing and treating low-back and pelvic pain during pregnancy
findings: Intervention evidence varies; no clear acupuncture vs sham benefit; some belt/exercise effects in individual studies.
funding: Review and trial funding not fully extracted
limitations: Old search; mixed pain definitions and low-quality comparisons; see P3-21/22

title: Effect of hypopressive and conventional abdominal exercises on postpartum diastasis recti: A randomized controlled trial
findings: No clear difference between hypopressive and conventional exercise groups.
limitations: No claim premium hypopressive program is superior; absolute estimates and spontaneous recovery pending
